children: By Staff Writer

The Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL) project has sought additional financing from the World Bank to extend its six-year lifespan and enable it to complete and upscale ongoing projects across the 19 Northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The Bauchi State ACReSAL Project Coordinator, Dr Ibrahim Kabiru, disclosed this while speaking with journalists on the sidelines of a five-day hybrid Additional Financing (AF)/Pre-Appraisal Mission meeting held at the Ahmadu Bello International Conference Centre in Bauchi on Monday.

Kabiru said the need for additional financing followed the outcome of the project’s Midterm Review (MTR), which showed that funds initially budgeted for the six-year programme had been exhausted, leaving some ongoing projects at risk of being abandoned before completion.

He said, “Hybrid Additional Financing for ACReSAL, what this means is that the project is now about four years old. It has a lifespan of six years. We conducted our MTR, or midterm review in the last few months, and we realised that most of the projects that we have started will be likely not be completed because we have already exhausted the money that has been budgeted for the six years partnership.”

According to him, the ACReSAL team subsequently engaged the Federal Government, which is the borrower, and the World Bank, the lender, to seek an extension of the project through additional financing.

He said, “So based on the MTR and the performances of the 19 Northern States and FCT, ACReSAL team liaised with the Federal Government, which is the borrower, and also reached out to the World Bank, the lender, and agreed that the project be extended through additional financing.”

Kabiru added that the ongoing five-day meeting was aimed at identifying areas that require additional funding and the requirements for the 19 Northern states and FCT to participate in the additional financing programme.

“At this point, we are not sure what awards we can get from the World Bank. So we need to gather, across all the states, together, and that’s why we have started here in Bauchi, to discuss about those areas that require this money and those requirements that are needed from the 19 Northern States and FCT to participate in the additional financing,” he said.

The project coordinator said representatives of the 19 Northern states and FCT, the World Bank team, the three Task Team Leaders and the ACReSAL national office, led by the National Project Coordinator, were participating in the meeting.
He said the participants would review the project’s previous performance, assess proposals and identify projects and components that could be upscaled under the additional financing arrangement.

Kabiru said, “So, the 19 Northern States and FCT are here in Bauchi with their leaderships, the World Bank team, all the three Task Teams Leaders (TTLs) are here in Bauchi, and the National Office headed by National Project Coordinator are also here, to spend five days, starting from today up to Friday, to review our previous performances, look at our proposals, what we have already done, what are the projects that we want to upscale, our projects, the components of ACReSAL.”
He added that the meeting would provide a clearer picture of the expected additional financing and the steps required to access it.

“This is the rationale behind this engagement, and we are hoping that at the end of this engagement by Friday, we will be able to have a clear picture of what are we going to expect from the World Bank, what is the step going to implement, what is the step have done, so that they can be allowed to upscale. So we are all here to discuss about the additional financing for ACReSAL project,” he said.
Why Bauchi was selected

Explaining why Bauchi was selected to host the appraisal meeting and described as one of the better-performing states under the project, Kabiru attributed it to the state’s early commencement and implementation of ACReSAL projects.

He said, “It’s very simple, the Governor, Sen Bala Abdulkadir Mohammed has already mentioned it, ACReSAL implementation started here in Bauchi on 28th of May 2023. Bauchi was the first state that launched it across all 19 Northern States and FCT.”

He added that Bauchi had implemented several projects considered among the better-performing interventions under ACReSAL, making the state suitable for the World Bank and Federal Government’s appraisal mission.

“And precisely, if I can put it on record, the World Bank and also the Federal Government can tell you that we implemented a lot of projects under ACReSAL that were among the most performing states. And that’s why the World Bank and also the Federal Government decided to come to Bauchi for this appraisal,” he said.
Kabiru said the appraisal would not be limited to discussions at the conference centre, as the participants would visit project sites across the state to assess completed interventions.

According to him, “We are not going to stay entirely in the hall. We are going to visit so many locations to see the tangible projects that were executed. And Bauchi is among the states that has these tangible projects that we have visited, and they can serve as a back-up to get additional financing, and that’s the essence of coming to Bauchi for this additional financing.”

title: ZAWYA: Nigeria seeks additional World Bank funding for climate resilience projects
